pharm: Synthetic pyrethroid ectoparasiticide; disrupts arthropod sodium-channel gating to produce paralysis and death of lice and mites.
quick: Head lice: 1% rinse, leave 10 min; Scabies: 5% cream, leave 8-14 h
No adequate human data; minimal absorption, generally considered low risk
Minimal systemic exposure; generally considered compatible
Local itching/redness; treatment response (live lice/new lesions)
summary: Permethrin is a synthetic pyrethroid applied topically to kill lice and mites. The 1% creme rinse is an OTC treatment for head lice (Pediculus capitis), applied to washed, towel-dried hair and left on 10 minutes before rinsing. The 5% cream (Elimite/Acticin) treats scabies (Sarcoptes scabiei), applied from the neck down and left on 8-14 hours before washing off. It is for external use only.
indications: Head lice (Pediculus humanus capitis) and their eggs - 1% creme rinse

dosage.d: Saturate washed, towel-dried hair and scalp; leave on 10 minutes (no longer), then rinse with warm water
dosage.t: May repeat once in 7-10 days if live lice are seen
dosage.n: Begin applying behind ears and at nape of neck; comb out nits; not for children under 2 months

dosage.d: Massage thin layer into skin from the neck down over the entire body (including soles, between fingers/toes, under nails); leave on 8-14 hours, then wash off
dosage.t: Usually a single application; may repeat once in 7-14 days if living mites appear
dosage.n: In infants/elderly and immunocompromised, also treat scalp, temple, and forehead; one 30 g tube typically suffices for an average adult

admin: For external use only - avoid eyes, nose, mouth, ears, and vagina
1% rinse: wash hair with shampoo (no conditioner), rinse, towel dry until damp; shake bottle; saturate hair and scalp; protect eyes with a towel; leave 10 minutes then rinse
5% cream: apply to clean, dry, cool skin from the neck down; cover the entire body surface; leave on 8-14 hours (e.g., overnight) then wash off in bath/shower
Reapply 5% cream to hands if washed during the treatment period
Comb out remaining nits with the supplied fine-tooth comb after the 1% rinse
Wash bedding, clothing, and towels in hot water; vacuum to reduce reinfestation
moa: Permethrin is a synthetic pyrethroid that acts on the nerve cell membranes of lice and mites, disrupting voltage-gated sodium-channel function. Delayed channel repolarization causes depolarization, paralysis, and death of the parasite. It is both ovicidal and active against the adult/nymph stages.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to permethrin, any synthetic pyrethroid or pyrethrin, or chrysanthemums
Use on infants under 2 months of age (1% rinse)
relative: Allergy to ragweed (may cause breathing difficulty or asthmatic episode)
Inflamed, abraded, or broken skin (may increase absorption/irritation)
Lice in eyebrows or eyelashes - see a physician, do not apply
monitor: Persistent irritation, secondary infection, or breathing difficulty

preg: No adequate and well-controlled studies in pregnant women; systemic absorption after topical use is minimal (<2%). The 5% cream is often classified as relatively low risk; if pregnant or breast-feeding, consult a health professional before use.
lact: It is not known whether permethrin is excreted in human milk after topical use; systemic exposure is minimal. It is generally considered compatible with breast-feeding; some recommend briefly interrupting nursing or applying after a feed for the 5% cream.
renal: No dosage adjustment; negligible systemic absorption with topical use.
hepatic: No dosage adjustment; negligible systemic absorption (permethrin is rapidly metabolized and excreted).

serious: Eye irritation if product contacts the eyes
emergency: Breathing difficulty or asthmatic episode (especially in ragweed-allergic patients)

monitoring: Inspect for live lice and nits 7-10 days after the 1% rinse; re-treat if live lice persist
Reassess scabies at 1-2 weeks; persistent or new burrows/lesions may warrant repeat treatment
Watch for local irritation, redness, or signs of secondary infection
Note that post-scabietic itching can persist 2-4 weeks despite cure
counsel: For external use only; keep out of eyes, nose, mouth, ears, and vagina - flush with water if contact occurs
1% rinse: leave on hair only 10 minutes then rinse; comb out nits; repeat in 7-10 days only if live lice are seen
5% cream: apply from the neck down over the whole body, leave on 8-14 hours (overnight), then wash off
Treat close contacts and household members; wash bedding, clothing, and towels in hot water
Itching may continue for days to a few weeks after successful scabies treatment and does not necessarily mean failure
Do not use on children under 2 months without medical advice; tell your doctor if allergic to ragweed or chrysanthemums
pk: Kills lice/mites on contact during the application period
Minimal systemic absorption (<2% of applied dose)
Rapidly metabolized by ester hydrolysis; little systemic accumulation
Residual ovicidal/parasiticidal activity persists ~10-14 days on hair/skin
Store at 20-25 C (68-77 F); avoid freezing
pearls: 1% creme rinse is OTC for head lice; 5% cream (Elimite/Acticin) is prescription strength for scabies
Pyrethroid resistance in head lice is increasingly common - consider alternative agents if treatment fails despite correct use
For scabies, treat all household and close/sexual contacts simultaneously to prevent reinfestation
Persistent post-scabietic pruritus is expected for up to 2-4 weeks and should not be mistaken for treatment failure
Cross-reactivity: avoid in patients allergic to chrysanthemums, pyrethrins, or ragweed
Do not use a conditioner before the 1% rinse - it reduces pediculicidal activity
missed: Permethrin is used as needed rather than on a fixed daily schedule; there is no routine daily dose to miss. If a scheduled second application (in 7-14 days) is forgotten, apply it as soon as remembered. If a 5% cream application is washed off early, re-treat as soon as practical.
overdose: Topical overdose or excessive application may increase local irritation but rarely causes systemic toxicity given minimal absorption. If accidentally swallowed, get medical help or contact a Poison Control Center (1-800-222-1222) immediately; manage with supportive care. Flush eyes or skin with copious water for accidental contact.
